headline: High: Roo Code’s filesystem/MCP/browser defaults can amplify Firecrawl outputs into prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading action errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes MCP-compatible/API outputs; Roo Code can use MCP, run browsers, and read workspace files. That creates a default bridge where attacker-controlled scraped content can be reinterpreted as instructions. The interaction is documented by profiles, though not sandboxed, so uncertainty pushes severity up.
conditions: IF Firecrawl returns untrusted web text that Roo Code feeds into an MCP/tool prompt
IF Roo Code reads Firecrawl output from workspace files or browser content without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a strict instruction/data delimiter in the handoff prompt
Disable automatic tool execution on imported content
Route Firecrawl output through a sanitizer that strips imperative text
Use a read-only staging file for scraped content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every Firecrawl artifact

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl touches API keys and broad network egress; Roo Code reads and writes the VS Code workspace, uses MCP, and also has broad egress. If sensitive Firecrawl outputs land in the shared workspace, Roo Code can exfiltrate them through its model/API calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default setups and the blast radius includes secrets.
conditions: IF Firecrawl writes scraped secrets or API-key-bearing artifacts into the shared workspace
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Keep Firecrawl outputs outside the VS Code workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
Restrict Roo Code to a dedicated empty workspace
Disable MCP servers that can forward file contents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl can run multiple instances and has broad network egress; Roo Code supports multiple instances, writes the filesystem, and modifies git state with shared state via filesystem. Both agents can mutate overlapping workspace artifacts, so concurrent writes and git-state races are plausible by default and can corrupt work or commits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or repository
IF Firecrawl output is written into files that Roo Code edits or commits
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees for isolation
Lock shared files during handoff
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped web content and structured data; Roo Code can treat workspace content as input and has tool authority to edit files, run browsers, and execute shell commands. If Roo Code trusts Firecrawl output without verification, bad facts or malicious instructions can cascade into incorrect code changes or actions. The pairwise pathway is directly supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Firecrawl output as authoritative without a verification step
IF Firecrawl output is converted into code, shell commands, or browser actions
mitigations: Require a human review step before execution
Compare Firecrawl claims against a second source
Mark Firecrawl output as untrusted in prompts
Limit Roo Code to read-only analysis mode for imported content
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles web content and API keys, while Roo Code handles source code and browser screenshots with broad filesystem and network access. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a concrete compliance breach cannot be proven; however, shared handling of sensitive data classes and broad egress creates a plausible retention/logging mismatch risk. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF either agent logs or retains scraped content longer than the other
IF regulated data is placed into Firecrawl outputs and then processed by Roo Code
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Review both agents’ retention settings
Disable verbose logging for both agents
Store outputs in a short-lived scratch directory
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
